summary: Configured node1 (OPNsense) to route between lan-a (node1<->node2, 10.60.10.0/24) and lan-b (node1<->node3, 10.60.20.0/24) by creating opt1/opt2 interfaces on vtnet1/vtnet2, assigning static routed IPs on node2/node3 via NetworkManager, and adding a single OPNsense port alias "node3_svc_ports" (8080, 8443, 9000) referenced by one firewall pass rule permitting node2->node3 TCP traffic on that alias (not one rule per port). Also fixed a secondary blocker: node3's local firewalld was rejecting the forwarded traffic even though pf correctly forwarded it; opened the three ports in firewalld on node3. Verified the three named ports work, an out-of-set port (9999) stays blocked, and the reverse direction (node3->node2) is blocked by default-deny. All three nodes were then restarted one at a time; boot identity change was proven via kern.boottime (node1, FreeBSD) and /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id (node2/node3, Linux), and post-restart the alias, pf rule, interface addressing, static routes, and firewalld port openings all persisted, with a full end-to-end functional re-test passing after the last restart.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (OPNsense/FreeBSD) interfaces and config.xml; found only 'lan' (vtnet0) assigned, vtnet1/vtnet2 unconfigured
Inspected node2/node3 NICs (enp1s0 management, enp8s0 unconfigured second NIC); confirmed RHEL9 with NetworkManager and firewalld active
Added opt1 (LANA, vtnet1, 10.60.10.1/24) and opt2 (LANB, vtnet2, 10.60.20.1/24) interfaces to node1's config.xml and applied via configctl interface reconfigure
Assigned static IPs via nmcli on node2 (10.60.10.2/24 enp8s0) and node3 (10.60.20.2/24 enp8s0), plus specific routes to the peer lan subnet via node1 (avoided a second conflicting default route)
Confirmed via ping which node mapped to opt1 (node2/lan-a) vs opt2 (node3/lan-b)

Created OPNsense port alias 'node3_svc_ports' (8080,8443,9000) under the correct OPNsense/Firewall/Alias model path in config.xml (initial attempt at legacy top-level <aliases> was wrong for this OPNsense version and silently failed pf compilation; corrected and verified with pfctl -sr)

Added a single firewall pass rule on interface opt1 (source 10.60.10.2 / node2, destination 10.60.20.2 / node3, port = alias node3_svc_ports, protocol tcp) and reloaded pf via configctl filter reload, preserving the existing SSH/management pass rules on vtnet0

Diagnosed a false 'no route to host' failure: SYN packets were correctly forwarded by node1's pf onto vtnet2, but node3's local firewalld public zone rejected them (ICMP admin-prohibited); opened 8080/8443/9000 in firewalld on node3 and reloaded

Verified functional behavior with python3 http.server test listeners: node2->node3 succeeds on 8080/8443/9000 (HTTP 200), fails on 9999 (not in alias); node3->node2 on 8080 is blocked (no packet reaches node1's opt2), confirming default-deny/directionality
Captured healthy baseline (boot markers, interface/route state, pf rules, firewalld ports) on all 3 nodes

Restarted node1 via 'shutdown -r now' backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect; polled until reachable; confirmed changed kern.boottime; verified opt1/opt2 addressing, ip forwarding, and pf alias rule all persisted; re-ran end-to-end HTTP test node2->node3:8080 successfully

Restarted node2 via backgrounded 'systemctl reboot'; polled until reachable; confirmed changed /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id; verified enp8s0 static IP and specific route to lan-b persisted; re-ran end-to-end HTTP test successfully

Restarted node3 via backgrounded 'systemctl reboot'; polled until reachable; confirmed changed /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id; verified enp8s0 static IP, route to lan-a, and firewalld port openings persisted; re-ran full end-to-end test for all three ports plus the blocked out-of-set port
Cleaned up temporary test HTTP listeners and log files on node2/node3

evidence.requirement: Single named port-object (alias) covering TCP 8080/8443/9000, referenced by the firewall rule instead of per-port rules
evidence.summary: config.xml/pf shows one alias 'node3_svc_ports' = {8080,8443,9000} and a single pass rule on opt1 referencing the alias by name, compiled by pf into three port-specific pass lines all sharing the same rule label.

evidence.requirement: node2 can reach node3 on TCP 8080, 8443, 9000 through node1's routing+firewall
evidence.summary: curl from node2 to 10.60.20.2 returns HTTP 200 on all three ports; tcpdump on node1 shows the SYN traversing vtnet1->vtnet2 and being forwarded.

evidence.requirement: Only the three named ports are permitted; other ports/directions remain default-deny
evidence.summary: curl to port 9999 (not in the alias) fails with no response; reverse direction node3->node2 on port 8080 times out with no packet reaching node1's opt2 interface.

evidence.requirement: node1 healthy baseline before restart (interfaces, forwarding, pf rules) and boot identity
evidence.summary: Captured kern.boottime=17:19:30, ip forwarding=1, and active pf pass rules for the alias-based policy prior to restart.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and post-restart recovery
evidence.summary: Reboot acked before disconnect; SSH timeout confirmed the node went down; kern.boottime changed to 17:32:52 confirming actual reboot; opt1/opt2 addressing and the alias-based pf rule were intact post-boot; end-to-end HTTP test to node3:8080 succeeded afterward.

evidence.requirement: node2 healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and post-restart recovery
evidence.summary: boot_id captured as 34027437... before reboot; reboot issued (stream closed as expected for Linux reboot); connection timeout confirmed downtime; boot_id changed to df91e99b... after recovery; static IP/route to lan-b persisted; end-to-end HTTP test to node3:8080 succeeded afterward.

evidence.requirement: node3 healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and post-restart recovery including firewalld port state
evidence.summary: boot_id captured as 555221a1... and firewalld ports 8080/8443/9000 confirmed open before reboot; reboot issued; connection timeout confirmed downtime; boot_id changed to 3b5d49a9... after recovery; firewalld ports, static IP, and route to lan-a persisted; full end-to-end test post-restart showed 8080/8443/9000 succeeding and 9999 correctly blocked.
